message.content:
**C♯ Major Scale**

The C♯ major scale follows the pattern of whole‑whole‑half‑whole‑whole‑whole‑half steps (W‑W‑H‑W‑W‑W‑H).  
Starting on C♯, the notes are:

| Scale Degree | Note |
|--------------|------|
| 1 (Tonic)    | C♯ |
| 2 (Supertonic) | D♯ |
| 3 (Mediant) | E♯ (which is enharmonically equivalent to F) |
| 4 (Subdominant) | F♯ |
| 5 (Dominant) | G♯ |
| 6 (Submediant) | A♯ |
| 7 (Leading tone) | B♯ (enharmonically equivalent to C) |
| 8 (Octave) | C♯ |

So the full C♯ major scale is:

**C♯ – D♯ – E♯ – F♯ – G♯ – A♯ – B♯ – C♯**

(If you prefer to use the enharmonic equivalents, it can also be written as: C♯ – D♯ – F – F♯ – G♯ – A♯ – C – C♯.)
